tasks.short: Check hours and pay adjustments and post them in AFAS.

today.trigger: Every morning after the previous day's shifts close, and again in the days before the monthly payroll cutoff.
steps: Open AFAS time records and the rosters for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Compare clocked hours with the planned shift and with corrections a team lead sent by mail or Excel.
Check overtime, night and weekend allowances against the transport CAO or the warehouse CAO on that contract.
Chase missing clock-outs and unsigned corrections in Teams or Outlook.
Post the accepted hours and adjustments onto the payroll records.
drudgery: Retyping hour lines from a site spreadsheet into AFAS.
Matching nicknames and badge numbers to employee numbers.
Repeating the same missing clock-out reminder to team leads.
today.time_sinks: Waiting on Tilburg and Venlo for one missing out-clock, then re-checking people whose hours were already correct.

lenses.faster: Clock, roster and allowance codes are matched before the specialist opens the file, and the clean rows are already posted. The morning pass through every name disappears.
lenses.autonomous: When a shift closes, a job compares clocks, the roster and open corrections and posts every row inside the CAO rule for that contract. The job starts from the shift close.
lenses.ambitious: All three sites would be checked every day, own staff and the agency hours worked beside them, against the correct CAO. A missed shift allowance would show up the same week, while the team lead still remembers the shift.
lenses.joy: Copying spreadsheets and chasing clock-outs is the part nobody would miss. What remains is a judgment on a disputed night shift or a dock clock that failed.
lenses.options: Each gap is shown as a forgotten clock-out, paid handover, wrong cost centre, an agency worker on an own badge, or a roster error, with the pay line each one would create. The specialist accepts the one the team lead confirms.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets which hour types may post on their own and which must stop, then reviews the weekly exception rate per site and tightens the rule that fails most often.
reach: The bookkeeper's match of agency hours to the three staffing-agency invoices.
The HR administrator's update of contract hours when someone changes shift pattern.
The site planner's comparison of rostered hours with hours actually worked.

tasks.human_edge: Decides whether an odd shift was really worked when the clock and the team lead disagree, and owns the conversation when a correction reduces someone's pay.
tasks.pattern_why: Hours, rosters and CAO allowance windows are structured, and a posted row either matches those sources or it does not. A coded check can post the clean rows and leave a short exception list that a person can explain to an employee, the works council or an auditor.

in_practice.trigger: Each shift close, plus a final pass on the last working day before the monthly cutoff.
steps: Read clocks, the approved roster and the contract CAO group from AFAS for that shift.
Apply the allowance windows and overtime rule configured for that CAO.
Post rows that match and that sit inside contract hours plus the agreed overtime threshold.
Open one task per remaining row, showing the records that disagree, and assign it to the team lead.
Post the confirmed correction onto the payroll record before cutoff.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves adjustments above the agreed threshold, any row a team lead disputes, and the cutoff batch. Matched hours inside the rule post on their own.
data_needed: Clock-in and clock-out per employee, with site and cost centre.
The published roster for that shift.
Contract CAO group, hours, scale and site.
Allowance and overtime rules stored as AFAS wage components.
Team-lead corrections with a reason code.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS time and payroll record for the shift, with the rule version and the name of anyone who approved an exception.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit can register worked hours and pass them into payroll as wage components.
Shift allowances and overtime can be written as tables by CAO, time window and contract group, and a payroll engine can apply those tables.
A Dutch works council has a consent right over arrangements for recording attendance, behaviour or performance, so a new clock check needs the OR involved before go-live.

risks: A wrong allowance rule posts the same error onto every night shift until someone complains.
Treating the roster as fact when a clock fails pays a shift that was not worked.
Using the check to score lateness would change the purpose from pay to behaviour monitoring and would need works-council consent under the WOR and a fresh AVG basis.
Sick hours booked as worked, or the reverse, corrupt both pay and the verzuim record.
research_questions: Do Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo record clocks in AFAS today, or does a supervisor still send Excel?
What share of daily hour lines was posted unchanged over the last three months, and what were the correction reasons?
Which transport and warehouse allowances are already wage components in AFAS, and which are still keyed from memory?
Is there a current works-council agreement that covers time registration and who may see clock times?

tasks.short: Calculate wages and deductions and enter them in AFAS.

today.trigger: The monthly payroll cutoff, plus each batch of one-off items that arrives during the month.
steps: Collect items that are still outside AFAS: declarations, one-off CAO payments, advances, attachments of earnings and corrections.
Enter the wage components per employee.
Run the trial payroll and compare totals with last month and with headcount.
Fix the lines that break and run the trial again.
Release the final calculation so the journal and the payment file can be made.
drudgery: Keying the same allowance codes that the hour records already imply.
Rebuilding a variance workbook from the trial run.
Re-running the whole calculation after one late correction.
today.time_sinks: Late one-off items from managers, and attachments of earnings whose paperwork arrives mid-run.

lenses.faster: Gross-to-net stays in AFAS. Components that upstream hour and contract records already support are entered by the job, and the specialist opens a variance pack.
lenses.autonomous: On cutoff, AFAS runs the trial calculation from posted hours, standing contract data and approved one-off items. The specialist receives the pack when the run finishes.
lenses.ambitious: A trial run every week for shift staff, so month-end confirms a known result. Attachments of earnings, holiday-allowance accrual and both CAOs would be treated correctly every period.
lenses.joy: Keying repeated toeslag codes is the part nobody would miss. What remains is a strange net-pay result, and the decision to hold one payment.
lenses.options: Each outlier is shown against last month, against the contract and against the other CAO reading that a manager has claimed. The specialist sees the net effect of each reading before the run is released.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the wage-component catalogue and the checks a run must pass, and reviews the components that cause corrections. Operating the buttons of a standard run falls away.
reach: The compensation specialist's maintenance of CAO scales, steps and allowance rules in AFAS.
The controller's payroll journal, holiday accrual and holiday-allowance accrual.
The bookkeeper's handling of the SEPA payment file and bank returns in Rabobank.

tasks.human_edge: Releases the payroll run and remains the person behind the wage-tax return. Handles attachments of earnings, the protected minimum net (beslagvrije voet), and any net pay the checks cannot explain from the contract.
tasks.pattern_why: Dutch gross-to-net is a table-driven calculation AFAS already performs from wage components, tax credits and premiums. The work left is getting the right components in and accepting the trial run. A language model in the calculation would make the payslip harder to defend.

in_practice.trigger: Weekly trial for shift populations, and the monthly cutoff for the official run.
steps: Take posted hours, contract wages and approved one-off components as the only inputs.
Let AFAS calculate tax, employee insurance, pension and net pay.
Produce a variance pack: headcount, gross, allowances, net and employer cost against last period, by site and CAO.
Hold lines that move more than the agreed tolerance, or that carry an attachment of earnings.
After approval, close the run so Finance can post the journal and prepare the Rabobank batch.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves the variance pack and releases the run. Attachments of earnings, new deduction orders and any line the pack cannot explain stay manual. Sending the SEPA batch to Rabobank stays a separate approval.
data_needed: Posted hours and wage components for the period.
Contract scale, step, hours, CAO group and tax-credit choice.
Pension and premium settings already in AFAS.
Bailiff orders and the current beslagvrije voet for anyone under attachment.
Last period's totals by site and CAO.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS pay-run dossier: inputs, trial run, approver, final run and the journal reference. That dossier is the payroll record, kept with the statutory retention period.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit calculates Dutch gross-to-net from wage components, including wage tax and statutory premiums, and can produce a journal and a payment file.
Attachments of earnings have to respect a protected minimum net, and the deduction order is a legal rule a standard component can misapply if the bailiff's document is not read.
The employer remains responsible for the monthly wage-tax return that follows from the payroll calculation.

risks: An automated component that is slightly wrong scales across every warehouse shift in the same CAO group.
A transport contract and a warehouse contract coded with each other's allowance table will look tidy in the total and be wrong on the payslip.
Closing the run before late sickness or a late leaver forces a correction run and a second payment file.
Putting the calculation in a spreadsheet or a chat transcript creates a second record beside AFAS.
research_questions: Which wage components are still keyed by hand each period, and which source document do they come from?
How many trial runs does a typical month take, and which corrections cause the reruns?
How are attachments of earnings recorded today, and who checks the beslagvrije voet?
Are the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO separate employer contexts in AFAS, or wage scales inside one administration?

tasks.short: Keep holiday, ADV and sick leave correct for pay.

today.trigger: Manager approvals of leave during the month, sickness reports, and the monthly payroll cutoff.
steps: Record holiday, ADV, special leave and unpaid leave against the right balance.
Record sick hours and the pay percentage that applies in that phase of the absence.
Watch for statutory days that will expire, negative balances and sick time booked on top of holiday.
Answer employees and managers who disagree with a balance.
Pass the balances and the sick-pay effect into the payroll run.
drudgery: Rebuilding a personal tracker of ADV and statutory days because AFAS and Excel disagree.
Answering the same balance question from three sites.
Manually switching the sick-pay percentage when a long absence crosses a CAO threshold.
today.time_sinks: Disputes that turn out to be a wrong leave type, and long-term sickness files where partial return hours arrive late.

lenses.faster: Approved leave and absence update the balance and the pay effect when they are approved. The specialist's side spreadsheet of days left disappears.
lenses.autonomous: A nightly job lists leave that will expire, negative balances, holiday overlapping sickness, and sick periods that have crossed a pay-percentage step in the CAO table.
lenses.ambitious: Every employee would see a balance that matches payroll, and statutory days would be taken in the legal order before they expire. Partial return after illness would change pay in the first week it happens.
lenses.joy: Maintaining the May workbook of leftover ADV is the part nobody would miss. What remains is a real conversation when a balance looks wrong to someone who is ill or about to leave.
lenses.options: For a leaver or a long absence, the pack shows payout, taking the days, and holding a disputed balance, each with gross and net. HR can tell the employee the number that payroll can actually pay.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets the leave types, expiry rules and sick-pay steps in AFAS and reviews the exceptions. Keeping a personal tracker falls away.
reach: The HR business partner's timeline under the Wet verbetering poortwachter, on the pay consequences of week 52 and week 104.
The controller's holiday-pay liability at month close.
The manager's self-service approval of ordinary leave requests.

tasks.human_edge: Agrees balance corrections and leave payouts, and checks partial return to work against the hours HR and the manager have agreed. Diagnosis and the reintegration plan stay with HR.
tasks.pattern_why: Leave types, expiry and sick-pay steps are rules with structured inputs and a balance that can be recalculated. AFAS already stores leave and absence. The specialist's value is the exception and the CAO table, both of which can be checked without a model.

in_practice.trigger: A manager approves leave, HR records an absence or a partial return, and a nightly expiry check.
steps: Write approved leave to the balance for that leave type and CAO group.
Apply the sick-pay percentage from the agreed table using absence hours and the week of absence.
Restore holiday hours when sickness during approved holiday is accepted.
List balances that will expire, go negative or disagree with the contract hours.
Feed the resulting paid and unpaid hours into the payroll inputs.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves balance corrections, payouts on leaving, and any sick-pay percentage the CAO table does not already set. Partial-return hours need the specialist's check before they change pay.
data_needed: Approved leave by type, day and hours.
Absence periods with hours and percentage of hours resumed, and no diagnosis text.
The CAO table for statutory leave, extra leave, ADV and sick-pay steps.
Contract hours and CAO group.
Expiry rule for each leave type.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS leave and absence records, and the payroll result that used them. A correction stores the approver and the reason on the employee dossier.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit administers leave and absence and can apply both in the payroll calculation.
Statutory vacation days generally expire six months after the end of the accrual year, while extra-statutory days usually last longer unless the CAO shortens that.
During the 104 weeks of the Wet verbetering poortwachter the employer continues pay at the percentage the contract and CAO set, including during partial return.

risks: Sending diagnosis text or a reintegration plan into a general assistant would process health data outside the absence file.
An automatic balance correction can change days an employee has already seen in self-service.
The warehouse CAO and the transport CAO can set different sick-pay percentages and different ADV rules.
A change to leave booking rules can require works-council consent before it is applied.
research_questions: Do employees request leave in AFAS self-service today, or by mail and spreadsheet?
How often is a balance disputed, and is the cause a data error or a CAO reading?
Where is the sick-pay percentage table held, and who changes it when an absence crosses a CAO step?
How does Finance take the holiday and holiday-allowance liability from payroll at month close?

tasks.short: Update tax credit, transfers and leavers on the payroll.

today.trigger: A tax-credit form, a site transfer or a resignation reaches payroll by mail or PDF.
steps: Read the form or the mail from HR administration or the manager.
Change the employee in AFAS: tax credit, address, bank account, cost centre, scale, hours or end date.
Check the effect on the next run, including a leaver's final settlement.
File the document in the dossier.
If the change arrives after cutoff, park it for a correction run.
drudgery: Retyping an IBAN, an address or an end date from a PDF into AFAS.
Discovering that HR administration already typed the same change in another screen.
Rebuilding the final settlement from leave balances and holiday allowance when someone leaves.
today.time_sinks: Transfers that arrive after the cutoff, and leavers whose last working day, leftover leave and holiday allowance do not agree.

lenses.faster: The mutation screen opens prefilled from the tax-credit form, the transfer or the resignation letter. The specialist compares the diff and saves.
lenses.autonomous: A signed change in the HR workflow opens a payroll task with the proposed field diffs as soon as the document is complete. The write waits for approval.
lenses.ambitious: A leaver's final settlement would be ready on the last day, with leave, holiday allowance and pro-rata pay already calculated. A transfer would move cost centre and CAO group in the same period the person moves.
lenses.joy: Retyping IBANs and end dates is the part nobody would miss. What remains is the conversation when a leaver disputes the final payslip.
lenses.options: A resignation shows three settlements side by side: leave paid out, leave taken before the end date, and a disputed balance held. HR sends the figure payroll can pay.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the mutation types and the checks on them: missing IBAN, two employers applying the tax credit, end date before the last worked day. Opening the right screen by memory falls away.
reach: The HR administrator's entry of contract changes, done once and checked by payroll.
The compensation specialist's scale and step when a transfer changes the job.
The bookkeeper's final payment and any equipment or advance deduction on leaving.

tasks.human_edge: Approves each change that affects pay, tax or the final settlement, and is the person who answers a leaver about that payslip. The four-eyes check on a new IBAN stays with a person.
tasks.pattern_why: The input is often a letter or a PDF, it touches several fields, and it changes what someone is paid or whether wage tax credit is applied. A workflow can propose the diff. It counts only after the specialist approves it in AFAS.

in_practice.trigger: HR workflow reaches 'signed' for a transfer, a tax-credit form or a resignation.
steps: Read the signed document from the employee dossier or the workflow.
Propose the AFAS field changes: tax credit, address, IBAN, site, cost centre, hours, scale, end date.
For a leaver, calculate pro-rata pay, leftover leave and holiday allowance from AFAS balances.
Show the diff and the next-payslip effect to the specialist.
Write the approved mutation and store the source document on the dossier.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves every mutation before it writes. A new IBAN needs a second person. Anything that does not match the signed document is sent back to HR administration.
data_needed: The signed tax-credit form, transfer or resignation.
Current AFAS employee, contract, leave balance and holiday-allowance balance.
CAO rules for payout of leave and holiday allowance on leaving.
Cost centre and CAO group of the destination site.
Who has already keyed the same change.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS mutation log with the approver's name, and the source document in the employee dossier. A chat transcript is not the payroll record.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit stores the employee and contract data payroll calculates from, including changes to contract and master data.
The employee tax-credit choice (loonheffingskorting) is a standard Dutch payroll field and is declared on the wage-tax form.
A final settlement typically settles pro-rata pay, unused leave and accrued holiday allowance; the exact payout follows the contract and CAO.

risks: Sending a BSN, an IBAN or a home address to a model outside the tenant would breach AVG minimisation. Any extraction has to run inside the company environment and keep no training copy.
A wrong tax-credit flag taxes the employee incorrectly for the rest of the year.
A wrong end date or leave payout creates a claim and a correction run.
HR administration and payroll both keying the same change will overwrite each other.
research_questions: What share of these changes already arrives as an AFAS workflow, and what share arrives as Outlook or PDF?
How many correction runs in the last two quarters came from a late transfer or a wrong end date?
Who may change an IBAN or the tax-credit flag today, and is there a second approver?
Does HR administration already enter these fields, so payroll is keying them a second time?

tasks.short: Find payroll differences and clear them before payday.

today.trigger: The trial payroll finishes, or a manager, employee or site reports a wrong payslip line.
steps: Review time sheets, shift patterns and the trial wage calculation for odd amounts.
Compare this period with last period in Excel, by employee and by total.
Open the employee and find the cause of each difference.
Ask the manager or team lead which reading is right.
Post the correction and check that the trial totals now tie.
drudgery: Scrolling through complete time sheets looking for the one line that feels wrong.
Rebuilding the same comparison with last month by hand.
Chasing three sites for an explanation the clock record already contains.
today.time_sinks: Differences that are real overtime or a real Sunday, mixed in with duplicates and missing cost centres, so every line takes the same effort.

lenses.faster: The review opens on a ranked list of breaks, each with the two records that disagree. Reading every time sheet and every payslip line disappears.
lenses.autonomous: Each trial run publishes the same checks and opens a task for every break: hours against contract, net against last month, allowance against the shift window, paid headcount against HR headcount.
lenses.ambitious: Breaks would be caught in the week they happen, on both CAOs and all three sites, so the monthly run has a short list. The company would have a complete payroll control file for the first time.
lenses.joy: Hunting through 750 lines for the one that feels off is the part nobody would miss. What remains is deciding a case the rule cannot see, and explaining it to the manager.
lenses.options: Each break shows the likely causes in order, and the payslip line each cause would change. The specialist can also see the cost of leaving it until next month.
lenses.altitude: The specialist writes the checks and the tolerance per wage component, and adds a check when the same break appears twice. Searching by eye falls away.
reach: The controller's tie-out of the payroll journal to the general ledger.
The accountant's month-close check on payroll accruals.
The people-analytics analyst's view of exception rates on the nightly Power BI extract.

tasks.human_edge: Decides whether a large allowance is a real shift or an error, and whether to correct, recover or explain it. Signs the control file that goes with the run.
tasks.pattern_why: The comparisons are arithmetic and joins across records AFAS already holds: hours, contract, wage components and last period. The output is a list of breaks with reason codes, which an auditor can re-run. Known patterns can propose a correction; they do not post it.

in_practice.trigger: Completion of each weekly trial and of the monthly trial run.
steps: Run a fixed set of checks on the trial result and the time records.
Classify breaks with a reason code where the pattern is known, such as a missing clock, a duplicate component or a contract that has ended.
Propose the correcting component for those known codes and leave it unposted.
Put unknown breaks, and any net movement above tolerance, on the specialist's list with both source records.
After the specialist accepts a correction, rerun the checks until the control totals tie.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves every correcting entry and the final control file. The check never changes a payslip on its own.
data_needed: Trial payroll by employee, wage component, site and CAO.
Posted hours and absence hours for the same period.
Contract status, hours and end date.
Last period's paid totals.
Agreed tolerances and reason codes.
in_practice.logs_to: The period's control file in AFAS, with each closed break, its reason code and the approver. The same file is what Finance can tie to the journal.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit can list payroll results and hours in a way a report or connector can compare across periods.
A payroll control that ties headcount, hours, gross and net to the previous period and to the ledger is ordinary finance practice and can be expressed as queries.
AFAS Profit exposes operational data through GetConnectors, which a report or the existing nightly extract can read.

risks: A tolerance that is comfortable on one salary hides a small error repeated across 400 warehouse employees.
Auto-posting the proposed correction would remove the control this task exists to provide.
If managers leave the queue untouched, the specialist is back to chasing, only from a different screen.
Turning the exception list into a ranking of employees would move it toward performance monitoring and the employment provisions of the EU AI Act.
research_questions: What were the top five causes of payroll corrections over the last six periods?
Which of those causes would a rule have caught on the trial run?
Do managers act on AFAS tasks today, or only on a mail from payroll?
What difference does Finance already accept between the payroll journal and the general ledger?

tasks.short: Fill in arrival and departure times for the pay period.

today.trigger: A shift ends with a missing clock, or a pay period opens for staff who do not clock.
steps: Collect paper sheets, site Excel files or incomplete clock records.
Fill arrival and departure from the sheet, the roster or a team lead's message.
Type those times into AFAS.
Send back sheets that are blank or unsigned.
Hand the completed times to the hours check.
drudgery: Copying arrival and departure off paper or out of a mailbox.
Guessing a departure time so the sheet is complete enough to pay.
Maintaining a different method for each site.
today.time_sinks: One site, or one group such as drivers or office staff, that has no usable clock and arrives as a pile at cutoff.

lenses.faster: Clocked staff already have arrival and departure on the record. Fixed-hours office staff follow their contract pattern unless an absence is open. Typing the sheet disappears.
lenses.autonomous: A missing out-clock opens a task for the team lead the same day. The time record stays incomplete until someone who was there confirms it.
lenses.ambitious: Every paid hour would have a source. Handover and waiting time, which the transport CAO can actually pay, would be visible as their own hour types.
lenses.joy: Little of this task is worth keeping. The useful remnant is a team lead confirming a shift they actually saw.
lenses.options: A gap is shown with three sources side by side: the clock, the roster and 'send back'. A guessed time is not one of the choices.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets who clocks, who is paid from a fixed pattern, and how fast a gap must close, then reviews the gap rate per site. Completing sheets falls away.
reach: The team lead's confirmation of a shift, which payroll currently reconstructs.
The HR administrator's list of who is in the clock population after a transfer.
The bookkeeper's need for the same gap rule on agency hours at that site.

tasks.human_edge: Agrees the population rules with HR and the works council, and accepts the rare shift a team lead confirms after a failed clock. Inventing a time to make the sheet complete is the habit this removes.
tasks.pattern_why: Arrival and departure are either a clock event or a fixed contract pattern. Both are structured and checkable. Filling a blank from memory is the failure mode, so the rule sends the blank back.

in_practice.trigger: A clock event arrives, a fixed-hours day opens, or a shift ends with a missing punch.
steps: Write clock-in and clock-out straight to the time record for staff in the clock population.
Write the contract pattern for office staff whose arrangement is fixed hours, unless absence is already recorded.
Leave any other gap empty and assign it to the team lead with the shift and the roster beside it.
Accept a team-lead confirmation as the source and store who confirmed it.
Pass only sourced times into the daily hours check.
in_practice.human_gate: The team lead confirms a missing punch. The specialist approves any population that moves from fixed hours to clocking, and any batch of reconstructed times. The roster alone never becomes a worked time.
data_needed: Clock events with employee number, site and device.
Contract pattern for staff who do not clock.
The roster, used as a comparison.
Team-lead confirmation and reason for each gap.
The works-council arrangement on who is clocked.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS time record, storing the source of each arrival and departure (clock, contract pattern or named team-lead confirmation).

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit can store clock-in and clock-out times and turn them into hours for payroll.
Recording attendance needs a works-council arrangement, because the OR has a consent right on systems that monitor presence.
Drivers' legal driving and rest records are a separate obligation from paid working time, so the two records have to stay distinct.

risks: Filling blanks from the roster pays people for hours they did not work and hides overtime they did.
Extending clocking to office staff without works-council consent will stop the rollout.
Overwriting a driver's paid hours with a reconstructed departure confuses pay and the legal driving-time record.
Clock data kept longer than the pay purpose, or visible to people who do not need it, fails AVG minimisation.
research_questions: Which groups have no clock today, and who fills their arrival and departure?
What share of shifts in the last month missed an in-clock or an out-clock?
Is there already a works-council agreement on time registration, and which populations does it name?
For drivers, do paid hours come from the planning board, from a driving-time record, or from both?

tasks.short: Enter new starters into payroll from their paperwork.

today.trigger: A signed contract arrives from the recruiter or HR administration, usually with a start date close by.
steps: Open the contract, the offer in Recruitee and the wage-tax form.
Create the employee and the contract in AFAS: hours, scale, step, CAO, site, start date and probation end.
Enter the tax-credit choice, bank account and identification result.
Check the first-period pro-rata amount against the CAO scale.
File the documents and confirm the person will be in the next run.
drudgery: Typing the same name, address, hours and scale from the contract into AFAS.
Hunting the offer in Recruitee because the PDF and the pipeline disagree.
Discovering a missing tax form on the Friday before a Monday start.
today.time_sinks: Seasonal peaks of starters, and first payslips that need a correction because scale, cost centre or tax credit was wrong.

lenses.faster: The new-hire screen is filled from the signed contract and the wage-tax form. The specialist checks the diffs and saves.
lenses.autonomous: When Recruitee shows the offer accepted and the contract is stored as signed, a payroll task opens with the proposed employee, contract and first-period pay. The payable record waits for approval.
lenses.ambitious: Every starter would be payable on day one on the right scale, cost centre and tax credit, including the seasonal wave. The first payslip would match the contract without a correction run.
lenses.joy: Typing the same address into several screens is the part nobody would miss. What remains is a clean first payslip, and the identification check the law puts on the employer.
lenses.options: Where the contract and the Recruitee offer disagree, both values are shown field by field with the first-period pay each would produce. The specialist pays the signed contract.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets which fields recruitment, HR administration and payroll each own, and reviews the rejects. Keying each starter falls away.
reach: The HR administrator's creation of the employee record, so it is keyed once.
The recruiter's offer data, which has to match the contract before payroll sees it.
The learning specialist's check that a mandatory certificate (forklift, VCA, food safety) is arranged before the first shift.

tasks.human_edge: Checks identity and the wage-tax form, including the BSN, and approves the record before anyone can be paid. Right to work is a human decision. The specialist also stops a start when the signed contract and the offer describe different pay.
tasks.pattern_why: A starter crosses Recruitee, a signed document and AFAS, and the first record determines tax, scale and pay. A workflow can assemble the draft. It becomes an employee in payroll only when the specialist approves it.

in_practice.trigger: Recruitee offer is accepted and the signed contract is in the dossier.
steps: Read the contract fields: name, start date, site, hours, CAO, scale, step, probation end and pay.
Compare them with the Recruitee offer and flag every difference.
Attach the wage-tax form and leave BSN, identity result and IBAN for the specialist to enter or confirm.
Show pro-rata pay for the first period from the CAO scale.
On approval, create the employee and contract in AFAS and place the person in the next run.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves each starter before the record can be paid. Identity, BSN and right to work are confirmed by a person. A mismatch between offer and contract goes back to the recruiter.
data_needed: Signed contract and the Recruitee offer.
Completed wage-tax form (opgaaf gegevens voor de loonheffingen).
Identity-check result, stored as a result.
IBAN, confirmed by the specialist.
CAO scale table and the destination cost centre.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS employee dossier and the workflow task that created it, including who approved it. Copies of identity documents stay in the controlled dossier.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit holds the employee and contract record that payroll pays from.
Recruitee holds the candidate, the pipeline and the offer that precede the signed contract.
Dutch employers identify the employee for payroll and collect a wage-tax form; the BSN is an identifier whose use is limited by law.

risks: A model that receives identity documents or a BSN outside the tenant breaks AVG and the limits on BSN use.
Automating the right-to-work decision would put an employment decision in the tool. The tool may only record a decision a person has made.
A wrong scale on a wave of warehouse starters repeats one error across many first payslips.
If HR administration already creates the AFAS employee, a second creation makes duplicates.
research_questions: How many own-staff starters does payroll enter in a normal month, and how many in the seasonal peak?
Which fields are retyped from Recruitee, and which already match the signed contract?
Does HR administration already create the AFAS employee before payroll opens it?
What share of first payslips over the last two quarters needed a correction, and for which field?

tasks.short: Collect hours, output and pay figures for the period.

today.trigger: Finance, a site or HR asks for period figures, and again at month close.
steps: Export hours and wage results from AFAS.
Collect the output sheets the sites send, such as trips or warehouse volumes, from Excel.
Paste the pieces into a workbook by site, cost centre and week.
Reconcile the workbook totals with the payroll journal by hand.
Send the workbook to Finance or drop it on SharePoint.
drudgery: Repeating the same export and pivot every period.
Renaming columns so Finance and HR mean the same thing by 'hours'.
Maintaining a workbook that the nightly Power BI model already partly replaces.
today.time_sinks: One site's output file arriving in a different layout, and totals that then refuse to tie to the journal.

lenses.faster: One dataset per pay period replaces the copy from time sheets, payroll and site spreadsheets. The specialist opens a report that already ties to the run.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS extract behind Power BI is extended with the hour types and wage-component totals payroll used to build by hand. It refreshes without a request.
lenses.ambitious: Hours, pay and site output would sit on the same cost centre every week, so overtime and agency use are visible while the week can still change. Labour cost at month close would start from that file.
lenses.joy: Maintaining the workbook is the part nobody would miss. What remains is reading the result and answering a sharper question from Finance.
lenses.options: The same totals are already cut by site, CAO, shift and hour type. A question that used to need a new workbook is a filter.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the definitions of clock hour, paid hour, absent hour and agency hour, and checks that Finance and HR use that set. Assembling the file falls away.
reach: The people-analytics analyst's nightly model, which payroll currently rebuilds in Excel.
The FP&A analyst's labour cost per site and per shift.
The bookkeeper's comparison of agency invoices with approved hours, kept as its own column.

tasks.human_edge: Agrees the definitions with People Analytics and Finance, and decides what a late site file means for the close. Publishing a number that mixes paid hours with output is the call the specialist keeps.
tasks.pattern_why: The compile is a join of structured payroll records to an agreed layout. Power BI already refreshes an AFAS extract every night. The work is to extend that extract and retire the workbook, which a query can do and a model should not rewrite.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly refresh, and the closing of each weekly trial and the monthly run.
steps: Publish hour type, wage component, site, cost centre and CAO from the AFAS run into the existing extract.
Load a site output file only when it maps to cost centre and week through an agreed layout.
Keep agency hours in a separate measure from own-staff paid hours.
Tie gross pay and hours in the dataset to the payroll journal before anyone uses it.
Leave the specialist a break list when a site file fails the layout or the tie-out.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist accepts a new or changed definition, and any period where the dataset does not tie to the journal. Routine refreshes publish on their own.
data_needed: AFAS hours by type, employee number, site, cost centre and CAO.
AFAS wage components and employer cost for the same grain.
The payroll journal totals for the tie-out.
Site output files in the agreed layout, where they exist.
Agency hours from the staffing portals, labelled as agency hours.
in_practice.logs_to: The dataset definition and the refresh log behind the Power BI model, including the journal total it tied to. Wide reports carry employee number, cost centre and role.

evidence.claim: The company already refreshes Power BI overnight from an AFAS extract, so a scheduled payroll dataset has a place to land.
AFAS Profit can expose payroll and hour data through GetConnectors for an external report.
A stable definition of paid hour versus clock hour versus agency hour is enough to replace a recurring consolidation workbook.

risks: Calling three different quantities 'hours' in one visual will send Finance and HR down a false difference.
The nightly extract misses late corrections unless the period stays open until the run is closed.
Site output files full of names, sent on to a wide audience, spread personnel data further than pay needs.
A cleanup step that silently drops a shift from a messy spreadsheet will still tie at the total and be wrong underneath.
research_questions: Which recurring workbooks does payroll still send, and who uses each one?
Does the nightly Power BI model already contain hour type and wage component, or only headcount and cost?
Where does site output data live, and can it be tied to a cost centre and a week?
How often do the compiled totals disagree with the payroll journal, and by how much?

role.altitude: The payroll specialist becomes the owner of the pay rules and the control file: the wage-component catalogue, the two CAO tables, the checks a run must pass, and the definitions of an hour that Finance and HR share. Month-end keying and personal spreadsheets fall away. The person signs the run, handles what the rules cannot close, and improves the check that failed.
reach: HR administrator: payroll-relevant contract changes and new-hire fields, keyed once and approved here.
Compensation and benefits specialist: CAO scales, steps and allowance rules maintained as AFAS wage components.
Bookkeeper: agency-hour invoices matched to the same approved hours, and the SEPA file toward Rabobank.
Controller: payroll journal, holiday accrual and holiday-allowance accrual at month close.
People analytics and HRIS analyst: the paid-hour and labour-cost definitions in the nightly Power BI model.
FP&A analyst: labour cost by site, shift and own staff versus flex, from that same dataset.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks are about half the year of this one FTE. The other half is payslip questions, the wage-tax return, the payment file, attachments of earnings, year-end statements and audits, and that half stays. The calendar does not compress: monthly cutoff, the 104 weeks of sick pay, the holiday-allowance payment, and three sites plus a seasonal flex wave. Freed hours make the control better and the close earlier. They do not create a second population one person can pay. One specialist who still holds the unwritten CAO readings in their head is a single point of failure for the controller and for 750 shift workers.
skills_to_grow: AFAS payroll setup: wage components, workflows, signals and GetConnectors.
Writing a check with a tolerance and a reason code, and reading the variance pack.
Turning a CAO clause into a table precise enough to configure and to test.
AVG minimisation and the works-council consent process for time registration.
Month-close language with Finance: accruals, cost centres, the SEPA batch and the wage-tax return.
role.ambitious_version: Pay for the shift population is under weekly control and the monthly run is a confirmation. Starters are payable on day one at the contracted scale, leave and sick pay follow the CAO without a side workbook, and the controller can tie the journal to a dataset People Analytics already refreshes. The specialist spends the freed time on the rules that still break: allowances, partial return from illness, attachments of earnings and final settlements. Own-staff pay and agency labour cost are visible in one place while the week can still be changed. A correct first payslip and quiet pay through day 90 is this role's contribution to the HR north star, and to a lower absence argument that started as a pay error.
